# docs_audit_report — 2026-11-20

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
I'd close the tab inside 20 seconds. The top headline hooks me, then the hero immediately dumps an audit retraction notice ("Repinned from v2 0.9857"), contradicts its own license (MIT-0 vs Apache 2.0), hides unlinked cherry-picked benchmarks behind broken progress bars, and finishes with five blog posts screaming about the project's own AI loop cheating and fabricating results.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. Self-sabotaging credibility collapse — Hero "Recent progress" card & `#writing` ("From the blog") expose audit retractions, cheating agents, and regex-disguised-as-NTK failures right next to unverified, unlinked 100% benchmark claims (`#results`).
2. Contradictory legal and technical claims — Hero badge & `<meta>` declare **MIT-0** while `<footer>` declares **Apache 2.0 License**; HumanEval gains jump between `+3.0pp`, `+15pp`, and `+18pp` across three cards with mismatched baselines and broken bar widths.
3. Insider-only jargon, ops-ticket copy, and broken HTML — `#results`, `#preprint`, and `#features` read like an internal autonomous-agent status log (`paper-v6`, `operator-initiated upload`, `FoVer`, `CCTU`, `CRANE`, `HalluGuard v3`, `KV260 FPGA`) and stray `</div>` tags literally eject the 7th capability card out of its grid.

## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- Top navigation bar (`<nav>`) — 12 text links + 2 external buttons (14 targets) in a single horizontal bar (`Get Started`, `Tutorial`, `Concepts`, `API`, `Problem`, `Capabilities`, `Results`, `Quick Start`, `Report`, `Paper`, `Writing`, `Roadmap`, `HuggingFace`, `GitHub`) — suggested cap: 5–6 top-level links.
- Whole-page card density — 33 cards total across the page (1 misplaced hero card, 2 problem cards, 4 how-it-works cards, 7 capability cards, 12 result cards, 7 blog cards) — suggested cap: <= 16 cards total on a landing page.
- Hero `.stats-bar` — jams a 58-word `.r-card` ("Recent progress") directly inside the 4-stat flex bar — suggested cap: 0 cards inside the stats bar; keep 3–4 crisp stat tiles only.
- `#results` ("What we measured") — 12 result cards, half of which are internal infrastructure/training/bugfix tickets rather than user-facing benchmarks — suggested cap: 4–6 core benchmark cards with sample size, baseline, model, and artifact link.
- `#writing` ("From the blog") — 7 blog cards, 5 of which are repetitive internal audit/failure post-mortems — suggested cap: 3–4 representative posts.
- Individual card body word counts — all bento cards stay under the 120-word cap (longest is "Why 'Energy-Based'?" at ~72 words), all `#results` cards stay under 60 words (they actually have *zero* body explanation), and the footer has no paragraph over 100 words; the bloat here is card-count and section sprawl rather than long paragraphs.

### Inconsistencies
- **License**: `<meta name="description">` and Hero badge claim `MIT-0` vs `<footer>` claims `Apache 2.0 License`.
- **HumanEval results**: `#features` ("Code") & `#results` card 1 claim `+3.0 points on pass-rate` (on 164-problem HumanEval) vs `#results` card 6 (`HumanEval-50`) claims `66% → 84% (+18pp)` vs `#results` card 8 (`HumanEval-50`) claims `70% → 85% (+15pp)` — three conflicting gains and two different baselines (`66%` vs `70%`) on `HumanEval-50` with no model or pipeline explanation.
- **FoVer AUROC vs "Why We Report Two AUROCs"**: Hero `.stats-bar` spotlights a single number `0.9131` (dual-condition) while the card beside it links to "Why We Report Two AUROCs Now" (`0.8947` architecture-only, repinned from `v2 0.9857`). Meanwhile `#results` card 7 cites a `0.125 FoVer baseline` on SVAMP with no explanation of how FoVer is both a flagship dataset/benchmark and a 0.125-AUC baseline.
- **"No fine-tuning / works with any LLM" vs GPU/weights requirement**: `#how` claims "No model fine-tuning required — Carnot works with any LLM you can call (Claude, GPT, Qwen, Gemma, local Llama)" vs Hero ships "model weights mirrored on HuggingFace", `#results` boasts "Two-GPU parallel retrain", and `#quickstart` says "so you can run them on a single GPU".
- **Gradient descent vs text prompting**: `#how` ("Why 'Energy-Based'?") claims the energy score provides "a gradient that the repair step can descend on" vs `#how` ("Repair") says Carnot simply "sends the specific violations back to the LLM as feedback" (black-box text prompting is not gradient descent).
- **Provenance claim vs actual cards**: `#results` intro states "Every number below is backed by a checked-in experiment artifact... labeled by provenance" vs **0 of the 12 cards** link to an artifact, state a model name, give sample size `n`, or show a provenance label.
- **Visual progress bars vs stated metrics**: `#results` card 1 (`+3.0 points`) draws `width: 14.6%`; card 2 (`+4.9 points`) draws `width: 66.7%`; card 11 (`4.4% cost savings`) draws a `95.6%` full green bar (`100 - 4.4`), visually misrepresenting a 4.4% gain as near-100%.
- **"Seven capabilities" vs content and DOM**: `#features` is titled "What you can check / Seven capabilities", yet cards 5 ("Research operations") and 6 ("APIs & portable memory") aren't things you check, and a stray `</div>` breaks card 7 ("Test-Time Compute (TTC) & PREM") completely outside `.bento-grid` (stray closing `</div>` tags also appear in Hero, `#problem`, and `#how`, while `#results` is missing a closing `</div>` for `.container`).
- **"Install and verify in five lines" vs actual code**: `#quickstart` has no install command in the code block, the Python example is 11 lines, the Rust example neither installs nor verifies an LLM (and references undeclared `&activations`), and `showTab()` relies on implicit global `event.target`.

### Missing essentials
- **Why should I trust the numbers?**: Zero links to artifacts, zero model names, zero sample sizes `n`, zero confidence intervals, and zero false-positive rates on any `#results` card — while the page itself advertises retractions, cheating agents, and an un-uploaded preprint.
- **How do I install it?**: `pip install carnot-ebm` is buried inside prose in the hero rather than as a copyable shell block in `#quickstart`, with no mention of Python version, JAX/CUDA vs CPU, Z3, or LLM API key setup. Rust installation (`cargo add` / crate versions) is completely absent.
- **What's the license?**: Contradictory (`MIT-0` at the top, `Apache 2.0 License` at the bottom), leaving legal usability completely unclear.
- **Who maintains it?**: Only a 50%-opacity footer line (`© 2026 Ian Blenke · Carnot Project`) with no maintainer bio, affiliation, contact channel, or community link — paired with "autonomous research loop" and "pending operator-initiated upload", it looks potentially unmaintained by humans.
- **Coherent scope in one sentence**: The hero gives a decent one-liner ("checks whether an answer is internally consistent — and suggests a fix when it isn't"), but the rest of the page fractures that identity across Z3/regex checks, FPGA Ising hardware, Langevin dynamics, constrained decoding, prompt-injection safety, and autonomous research agents without explaining what a user actually gets when they run `pip install carnot-ebm`.

### Fabrication signals
- `GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0` (`#results`, card 9) — literal **1.0 (100%)** true-positive rate with no sample size `n`, no false-positive rate, and no dataset link.
- `k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks` (`#results`, card 10) — **100% catch rate** on a tiny, self-styled (`PRM-BiasBench-style`) `n=60` sample with **no benign false-positive rate reported** (an AND-composed `k=5` verifier can trivially hit 60/60 by over-rejecting).
- `99.3% of wrong code flagged` (`#features`, "Code" card) — near-100% recall with no false-positive rate or precision reported, and strangely paired with only `+3.0 points` pass-rate improvement on HumanEval.
- `Zero false positives` across `639 experiments self-verified. 65 brace bugs auto-fixed.` (`#writing`, "Carnot Dogfooding by the Numbers") — exact **0.0 FPR** claimed on self-evaluation with no external check.
- `2.0× speedup, identical losses` (`#results`, card 5) — exact perfect linear scaling on 2 GPUs with "identical losses" (ignores communication overhead and floating-point non-determinism without explanation).
- `0.0pp accuracy delta with 4.4% cost savings` (`#results`, card 11) — exact `0.0pp` delta with no sample size or variance, visually inflated by a `95.6%` green bar.
- `0.90 AUC (vs 0.125 FoVer baseline)` (`#results`, card 7) — a **0.125** ROC AUC baseline is far worse than a 0.50 coin flip, signaling either an inverted/broken baseline, a mislabeled metric, or a strawman comparison.
- `7,768 Experiment runs / 382 Completed milestones / 30,658 Automated tests` (Hero `.stats-bar`) — massive volume counters right above blog posts admitting the autonomous loop fabricated a 95-microsecond 30B eval and wrapped 56 lines of regex in an NTK docstring; without independent verification, high counts look like automated noise rather than rigor.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The `#problem` ("LLMs predict. They don't check.") and `#how` ("Extract → Check → Repair") framing using the concrete `47 + 28 = 76` example explains the core concept clearly in plain English without hiding behind physics jargon.
- The Python `#quickstart` snippet (`VerifyRepairPipeline().verify(...)`) shows clean, immediately readable developer ergonomics, and the project's willingness to document its own retractions in the blog (if moved off the landing-page spotlight) is a rare sign of candor.
